claimText: Coffee has been classified as a cancer-causing agent by WHO

brave.title: IARC reclassifies coffee: no longer 'possibly carcinogenic'
brave.description: In 2016, the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) reclassified coffee, removing it from Group 2B ('possibly carcinogenic'). Coffee was placed in Group 3 ('not classifiable').

brave.title: WHO on coffee and cancer: What the science says
brave.description: IARC previously classified coffee as Group 2B in 1991 based on limited evidence. In 2016, after reviewing new evidence, IARC downgraded this classification, finding no conclusive link.

brave.title: Coffee and cancer: The complicated history of IARC classifications
brave.description: Coffee was listed as 'possibly carcinogenic' from 1991 to 2016. New evidence led to its reclassification. Current scientific consensus does not consider coffee a carcinogen.

brave.title: Nature: How IARC's coffee reversal reflects evolving cancer research
brave.description: IARC's 2016 reclassification of coffee illustrates how cancer risk assessments evolve with new evidence. The original 1991 classification was based on limited bladder cancer studies.

factCheck.text: Coffee is classified as cancer-causing by WHO

claimReviewMarkup.title: Context needed: IARC reversed its coffee classification in 2016
